345749.title: The ironic decoration conjecture
345749.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, let $d_v$ be the degree of $v$, and assign a number $f(v)$ to each vertex. Define $M(v)=f(v)d_v$. An assignment is **ironic** if $M(u)\ne M(v)$ for every adjacent pair $u,v$. **The ironic decoration conjecture.** Every graph $G$ has an ironic decoration by the set $\{1,2,\dots,\chi(G)\}$. The claim is trivially true for regular graphs, but remains open in general.

345750.title: The list cascade coloring conjecture
345750.statement: For a positive integer $k$ and a positive integer $r$, a **cascade** of length $k$ rooted at $r$ is the set $\{r,2r,\dots,kr\}$. **The list cascade coloring conjecture.** Every graph $G$ is colorable from arbitrary cascades of length $\chi(G)$. This generalizes the ironic decoration conjecture and remains open.

346691.title: The rainbow homogeneous-progression coloring conjecture
346691.statement: For $s,k\in\mathbb N$, let $A_{s,k}=\{s,2s,\ldots,ks\}$. A coloring is **rainbow** on a set when all elements of that set receive distinct colors. **Rainbow-coloring conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb N$ there is a $k$-coloring of $\mathbb N$ such that every set $A_{s,k}$ is rainbow. This problem was posed independently by Pach and Pálvölgyi; the source does not give a resolution.

346739.title: The conjectural recursive upper bound for Schur numbers
346739.statement:
For $n\ge 2$, let $S(n)$ denote the $n$th Schur number. **The recursive Schur-number upper-bound conjecture.**

$$
S(n)\le n\bigl(S(n-1)+1\bigr)\qquad\text{for all }n\ge 2.
$$

This conjecture follows from the preceding conjecture on $L(n)$ together with the paper's upper-bound theorem, and it is verified in the source for $2\le n\le 5$.

347082.title: The circular chromatic conjecture for planar graphs
347082.statement:
Let $t$ be a positive integer and let $G$ be a planar graph of girth at least $2t$. The **circular chromatic conjecture.**

$$
\chi_c(G)\le 2+\frac{2}{t}.
$$

The cases $t=1$ and $t=2$ follow from the Four Color Theorem and Grötzsch's theorem, respectively, while the conjecture remains open for every $t\ge 3$. It is known for $K_4$-minor-free graphs, a subclass of planar graphs.

347634.title: Defant–Engen–Miller's log-concavity conjecture for Lassalle's sequence
347634.statement:
Let $A_{k+1}(ell)$ denote the terms of the sequence introduced in the paper, with $k$ a nonnegative integer. **Defant3Engen3Miller's conjecture.** The sequence

$$
(A_{k+1}(ell))_{1 \le ell \le 2k+1}
$$

is log-concave for every nonnegative integer $k$. This is the main remaining open question after the paper proves unimodality of the relevant refinement; its log-concavity remains unresolved.

350664.title: Universal Gegenbauer expansion conjecture for graphical functions
350664.statement: Let $G$ be a graphical function for which the radial representation and Gegenbauer expansion are defined. **Universal Gegenbauer expansion conjecture.** The Gegenbauer expansion (gfr) is valid for all graphical functions. The statement extends the expansion beyond the classes established by the preceding results. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

351080.title: Ringel-type conjecture for degenerate graphs
351080.statement: Fix an integer $D$. **Degenerate-graph Ringel-type conjecture.** There exists $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $n\ge n_0$, if $G$ is a $D$-degenerate graph on $n$ vertices with $m\ge n-1$ edges, then $2m+1$ copies of $G$ pack into $K_{2m+1}$. The paper presents this as a possible analogue of Ringel's conjecture for degenerate graphs, but gives no resolution.

353438.title: The pleated bowtie spectral-rank conjecture
353438.statement:
Let $B_t$ denote the $t$-pleated bowtie graph, and let $\mathfrak{u}(B_t)$ be its spectral rank. **Pleated bowtie conjecture.** We have

$$
\mathfrak{u}(B_t)=1
$$

for $t\geq 8$. This claim extends the proved case $t=8$ established immediately before the conjecture; its status for all $t\geq 8$ is not resolved in the supplied text.

353680.title: The conjecture on infinitely many grids with discrepancy 2
353680.statement: Let $d_n$ denote the discrepancy associated with the grid of size $n$. **The discrepancy-2 conjecture.** There are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n=2$. In particular, for all $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $d_{2\cdot 3^k-1}=2$. This parallels Sutner's result that there are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n=0$; the statement is presented as unproved future work.

355100.title: Rainbow base factorization conjecture for 2-bounded partitions
355100.statement:
Let $M$ be a $k$-base matroid with $k\geq 3$, and let $\mathcal{P}$ be a partition of $E(M)$ satisfying

$$
|X|\leq 2
$$

for every $X\in\mathcal{P}$. **2-bounded rainbow factorization conjecture.** Then $M$ can be factorized into $k$ rainbow bases. This is presented as the first nontrivial special case of the broader bounded-partition conjecture; the source leaves it open.

355131.title: Kelly's conjecture on Hamiltonian decompositions of regular tournaments
355131.statement: A **regular tournament** is a tournament in which every vertex has the same indegree and outdegree. **Kelly's conjecture.** Every regular tournament on $n=2k+1$ vertices has a decomposition into $k$ arc-disjoint Hamiltonian cycles. The conjecture was proved for large $n$ by Kühn and Osthus; the source does not state a complete resolution for all $n$.

355207.title: Strong ionization conjecture for atomic Hamiltonians
355207.statement: Let $H_N$ be the $N$-electron atomic Hamiltonian with nuclear charge $Z\in\mathbb{N}$. **Strong ionization conjecture.** There is a universal constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $N>Z+C$, the operator $H_N$ has no eigenvalue. This would strengthen the ionization conjecture by ruling out all eigenstates beyond a uniformly bounded excess charge; the statement remains open.

355742.title: The polygonal stacked prism odd-prime labeling conjecture
355742.statement: Let $Y_{k,n}$ be the $k$-polygonal stacked prism with $k\geq 3$ sides and $n\geq 1$ polygons. **Polygonal stacked prism conjecture.** $Y_{k,n}$ is odd prime for all $k\geq 3$ and $n\geq 1$. The paper proves the result when $k$ is among several specific values, including powers of $2$, and conjectures the general case; constructing the required labeling for arbitrary $k$ remains open.

355743.title: The all-trees odd-prime labeling conjecture
355743.statement: Let $T$ be a tree. **All-trees conjecture.** Every tree $T$ is odd prime. Paths, unions of paths, star graphs, and several additional classes are known to be odd prime, but the assertion for all trees remains open.

356366.title: The exact constant conjecture for cycles of length two modulo $2k$
356366.statement:
For integers $\ell$ and $r$, let $c_{\ell,r}$ be the least constant such that every $n$-vertex graph with at least $c_{\ell,r}n$ edges contains a cycle whose length is congruent to $\ell$ modulo $r$.

**Exact constant conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 2$,

$$
\nc_{2,2k}=\frac{2k+1}{2}.
$$

The paper introduces this as a further conjecture for the case $\ell=2$; no resolution is given.

356437.title: NP-hardness conjecture for promise graph coloring
356437.statement: For integers $k\geq l\geq 3$, $\operatorname{PCSP}(K_l,K_k)$ is the promise problem of coloring a graph with $k$ colors under the promise that it is $l$-colorable. **Promise-coloring hardness conjecture.** For every $k\geq l\geq 3$, the promise problem $\operatorname{PCSP}(K_l,K_k)$ is NP-hard. The source states that this basic problem remains wide open.

357444.title: Normality conjecture for the binary sequence of binomial set partition values
357444.statement:
Let $a(n)$ be the integer sequence from Theorem, and define its binary reduction by

$$
\beta(n)=a(n)\bmod 2.
$$

A binary sequence is **normal** if every finite binary string of length $\ell\geq 1$ occurs in it with limiting frequency $2^{-\ell}$. **Normality conjecture.** The sequence $\beta(n)$ is normal.

358914.title: Percolation threshold conjecture for the 2-X-neighbor graph
358914.statement: For $d\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\theta^{\rm X}(2,d)$ denote the percolation probability of the $2$-X-neighbor graph on $\mathbb{Z}^d$. **Two-neighbor X-graph conjecture.** The $2$-XnG percolates for all $d\geq 3$ but does not percolate for $d=2$. Numerical experiments motivate this distinction, while the paper states that the corresponding cases remain unresolved.

359722.title: Aravind–Subramanian conjecture for the oriented chromatic number of bounded-genus graphs
359722.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of Euler genus $g$, and let $\chi_o(G)$ denote its oriented chromatic number.

**Aravind–Subramanian conjecture.** There is an absolute constant implicit in the $O$-notation such that

$$
\chi_o(G)=2^{O\left(\sqrt{g}\right)}.
$$

This removes the arbitrarily small positive term from the known bound $\chi_o(G)=2^{O(g^{1/2+\varepsilon})}$ for every constant $\varepsilon>0$.

359759.title: Existence of the linear-threshold generalized Ramsey limit
359759.statement:
Let $f(n,p,q)$ denote the generalized Ramsey number, and let $q_{lin}$ denote the linear threshold. **Linear-threshold limit conjecture.** The limit

$$
\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{f(n,p,q_{lin})}{n}
$$

exists for all $p\ge 3$.

This is a conjectural extension of the known cases $p=3,4$; existence for all $p\ge 3$ remains open.

360560.title: Subpolynomial growth for graphs without even decompositions
360560.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph without an even decomposition, and let $r_H(n)$ denote the graph parameter used in the paper. **Subpolynomial-growth conjecture.** For all graphs $H$ without an even decomposition,

$$
r_H(n)=n^{o(1)}.
$$

This is presented as a stronger statement than the conjecture attributed to Ge, Xu, and Zhang for cliques. Its status remains open in the paper.

360638.title: Height-two linear-extension universality conjecture
360638.statement: Let $m$ be a positive integer. **Height-two universality conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $m$, there exists a poset $P$ of height two such that $e(P)=m$. The source states that this conjecture would imply the coincidence-complexity result for height-two posets, but gives no resolution.

361002.title: The recursive upper-bound conjecture for tournament counting
361002.statement: For each positive integer $k$, let $c(k)$ denote the exponent for counting copies of an arbitrary $k$-vertex tournament. **Recursive counting conjecture.** For all $k \ge 3$ it holds that $c(k) \le c(k-1)+1$. The paper notes that this inequality is not obvious, unlike the corresponding inequalities for $c^*(k)$ and for a fixed tournament; no resolution is supplied.

361361.title: The general sparse induced-subgraph conjecture
361361.statement: Let $\operatorname{tw}(G)$ denote the treewidth of $G$. **The general sparse induced-subgraph conjecture.** For every $t\geq 1$, every graph of sufficiently large treewidth has an induced subgraph of treewidth $t$ which is either complete or $K_4$-free. The source presents this as a possible extension beyond even-hole-free graphs, motivated by known sparse obstructions; no resolution is given.

362758.title: The all-degree Hard Lefschetz conjecture for matroid Gorenstein rings
362758.statement: Let $M=(E,\mathcal I)$ be a matroid of rank $d$, let $\A(M)$ be its associated Gorenstein ring, and let $a\in\mathbb R^E_{>0}$. **All-degree Hard Lefschetz conjecture.** The ring $\A(M)$ satisfies $\HL_k$ for some $a\in\mathbb R^E_{>0}$ for every $k\leq\frac d2$. The paper subsequently states that this conjecture is false, so the proposed assertion is refuted.

362850.title: Parity-modulus conjecture for even progressions of odd-indexed $G_t$
362850.statement:
Let $t$ be odd, and write

$$
G_t(q)=\sum_{n\geq0}g_t(n)q^n.
$$

**Even-modulus conjecture.** If an arithmetic progression satisfies

$$
g_t(An+B)\equiv0\pmod2
$$

for every $n$, then $A$ is even. Thus, for odd $t$, any progression on which the coefficients of $G_t$ are all even must have even modulus. The source presents this as a conjectural pattern suggested by extensive computations.

363046.title: Dichotomy for saturation functions of sequences
363046.statement:
Let $u$ be a sequence, and let $\operatorname{Sat}(u,n)$ denote its saturation function on an alphabet of size $n$. **The saturation dichotomy.** For every sequence $u$, either

$$
\operatorname{Sat}(u,n)=\Theta(n)
$$

or

$$
\operatorname{Sat}(u,n)=O(1).
$$

This dichotomy is known for all sequences $u$ with two distinct letters, but remains open for sequences with more distinct letters.

363402.title: Stanton's monotonicity conjecture for $t$-core partitions
363402.statement:
Let $c_t(N)$ denote the number of $t$-core partitions of $N$. **Stanton's conjecture.** For all integers $t$ and $N$ satisfying $4\leq t\ne N-1$, one has

$$
c_t(N)\leq c_{t+1}(N).
$$

This conjecture strengthens the basic existence result for $t$-core partitions by predicting monotonicity in the core parameter; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text, so it remains open here.

363524.title: Reflection complexity periodicity conjecture
363524.statement:
Let $\mathbf{x}$ be a sequence. The **reflection complexity periodicity conjecture.**

$$
r_{\mathbf{x}}(n)=r_{\mathbf{x}}(n+2)\quad\text{for some }n
$$

if and only if $\mathbf{x}$ is eventually periodic. One direction is known: if $\mathbf{x}$ is eventually periodic, then the equality holds for all sufficiently large $n$. The conjecture asks whether the converse holds as well.

364185.title: Near-linear saturation conjecture for edge-ordered graphs
364185.statement:
Let $G$ be an edge-ordered graph, and let $sat_e(n,G)$ denote its edge-ordered saturation function. **Near-linear saturation conjecture.** For every edge-ordered graph $G$,

$$
sat_e(n,G)=O\left(n^{1+o(1)}\right).
$$

The paper identifies this as the main general upper-bound problem and notes that the same bound would imply the corresponding bound for $sat_m$.

364225.title: The quadratic lower-bound conjecture for minimal snake diagrams
364225.statement:
Let $L(n)$ denote the quantity measuring the size of a minimal snake diagram. **Quadratic lower-bound conjecture.** For all $n$,

$$
L(n)\geq \frac{n^2}{3}+an+b,
$$

for some constants $a$ and $b$. This conjecture asserts a quadratic lower bound for the size of minimal snake diagrams, but the supplied text gives no resolution.

364279.title: Grünbaum's orthogonal line equipartition conjecture
364279.statement:
Let $P$ be a convex body in the plane with area $1$.

**Grünbaum's conjecture.** For every $t\in[0,1/4]$, there exists a pair of orthogonal lines that partitions $P$ into four pieces whose areas, in clockwise order, are $t,t,(1/2-t),(1/2-t)$.

The conjecture is open in general, although the supplied context says it has been verified in certain special cases.

364886.title: Singer-type upper-bound conjecture for optimal Golomb rulers
364886.statement:
Let $G(k)$ be the length of an optimal Golomb ruler with $k$ marks. **Singer-type upper-bound conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq6$,

$$
G(k+2)<k^2+k.
$$

The source derives this as a consequence of the conjecture $H(I,I+2)=I(I+2)$ and notes that it would imply the stronger range-shifted form of the Erdős conjecture $G(k)<k^2$; the statement itself remains conditional and unproved.

365380.title: Gyárfás's tree-packing conjecture
365380.statement: Let $T_1,\ldots,T_n$ be trees such that $T_k$ has $k$ vertices for every $k$ with $1\leq k\leq n$, and let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices. **Gyárfás's tree-packing conjecture.** The trees $T_1,\ldots,T_n$ pack into $K_n$. The paper presents this as the conjecture it proves, so it is resolved by the source's claimed result.

366550.title: Zauner's conjecture on SICs in every dimension
366550.statement: Let a **$1$-SIC** be a set of $d^2$ distinct rank-$1$ Hermitian projectors in the algebra of linear operators on $^d$ satisfying the equiangularity condition. **Zauner's conjecture.** $1$-SICs exist for all $d$. This is the central existence conjecture for symmetric informationally complete measurements; the source does not state a resolution.

367029.title: Kong's modulo-$8$ conjecture for near-perfect matchings of odd square grids
367029.statement:
Let $a(2k+1)$ be the total number of near-perfect matchings of the $(2k+1)\times(2k+1)$ grid, and write

$$
a(2k+1)=2^k c_k.
$$

**Kong's modulo-$8$ conjecture.** For all $k$, the integer $c_k$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $8$.

This is presented as a further conjecture of Kong after the paper proves only that $c_k$ is odd; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

367231.title: Burr–Erdős–Lovász conjecture for chromatic Ramsey numbers
367231.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $R_\chi(G)$ be its chromatic Ramsey number, and define 
$$
M(n)=\min\{R_\chi(G):\chi(G)=n\}.
$$
 **Burr–Erdős–Lovász conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$, 
$$
M(n)=(n-1)^2+1.
$$
 The source states this conjecture as a theorem proved by Zhu, so it is solved.

367390.title: The conjecture that the sieve parameter satisfies $\widetilde{M}(k)=k$
367390.statement: Let $\widetilde{M}(k)$ denote the parameter in Theorem. **Conjecture on $\widetilde{M}(k)$.** One can take $\widetilde{M}(k)=k$ for all $k\geq 1$ in Theorem. This would improve the paper's conditional bounds and is motivated by a natural extension of Goldbach's conjecture; the source gives no resolution, so the assertion remains open.

367473.title: Lazebnik–Ustimenko–Woldar's girth conjecture for Wenger-type graphs
367473.statement:
Let $D(k,q)$ be the graph defined by the parameters $k$ and the prime power $q$. **Lazebnik–Ustimenko–Woldar's conjecture.** For every prime power $q\ge 4$, the graph has girth

$$
\operatorname{girth}(D(k,q))=
\begin{cases}
k+5, & k\text{ odd},\\
k+4, & k\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
$$

The source records matching lower bounds and presents equality as conjectural; no general resolution is supplied.
